dvobject structures by parser

Source: vignettes/articles/dvobject_structures.Rmd
dvobject_structures.Rmd

Every parser in dbparser returns a dvobject: a named list of tibbles (DrugBank’s are nested in lists by section) and a source_metadata record. This page lists, for each parser, the tables it returns, their columns and column types, the keys the parser checks, and the source record.

Nothing on this page is typed by hand. Each section runs the parser on the small example files bundled with the package (inst/extdata) when the page is built, and reads the tables, columns and types from the result. Row counts are those of the example files, not of the full databases.

The source_metadata fields are the same for every parser. Fields the source does not state, or that the caller did not pass (such as retrieved_at), are NA; nothing is guessed. They are read with get_source_metadata().

DrugBank: parseDrugBank()

The drug records of the DrugBank XML, grouped in lists: drugs (always), and with their options salts, products, references (articles, books, links and attachments, for drugs and for carriers, enzymes, targets and transporters) and cett (carriers, enzymes, targets and transporters, with their polypeptides and actions). Here every option is on, on the bundled small-molecule record.

The parser checks no key. Drug tables carry drugbank_id; CETT tables carry drugbank_id and the CETT id (e.g. target_id).

OnSIDES: parseOnSIDES()

The seven core relational tables of OnSIDES, named after their files, and high_confidence when that file is present.

The parser checks no key.

HPO: parseHPO()

Human Phenotype Ontology gene-phenotype associations as distributed by Harmonizome, with one row per gene and one per phenotype in the lookup tables.

The parser checks no key; associations holds distinct rows.

genes 7 gene_symbol (character), entrez_id (character), n_phenotypes (integer)
phenotypes 352 hpo_id (character), phenotype_name (character), n_genes (integer)

HGNC: parseHGNC()

The HGNC complete set (gene), every symbol and name of each gene (gene_name) and the withdrawn entries (withdrawn).

The parser stops unless hgnc_id is set and unique in gene. On the example files:

#>     gene_hgnc_id_unique gene_name_ids_are_genes 
#>                    TRUE                    TRUE

Health Canada DPD: parseHealthCanadaDPD()

The 13 tables of Health Canada’s read-me. Every table except inactive_products holds the rows of each product set requested, with extract naming the set.

The parser stops unless drug_code is unique in drug_product and every other table’s drug_code is a product. On the example files:

#> drug_product_drug_code_unique  every_drug_code_is_a_product 
#>                          TRUE                          TRUE

drug_product 12 drug_code (integer), product_categorization (character), class (character), drug_identification_number (character), brand_name (character), descriptor (character), pediatric_flag (character), accession_number (character), number_of_ais (character), last_update_date (Date), ai_group_no (character), class_f (character), brand_name_f (character), descriptor_f (character), extract (character)

openFDA: parseOpenFDA()

One table per record level of the Drugs@FDA (drugsfda_*) and NDC directory (ndc_*) downloads, field names as in the files.

The parser stops unless each table’s key is unique and every row names its parent row. The keys and parents it checks, read from the parser:
